Para facilitar la identificación de controles y funciones, Hable One ha desarrollado Stactiles, unas pegatinas táctiles que están ganando popularidad entre usuarios con discapacidad visual y que […] La entrada Stactiles: las pegatinas táctiles de Hable One que hacen accesible cualquier vitrocerámica se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las superficies táctiles han cambiado la forma en la que utilizamos muchos electrodomésticos, pero también pueden convertirse en una barrera para las personas ciegas o con baja visión. Para facilitar la identificación de controles y funciones, Hable One ha desarrollado Stactiles , unas pegatinas táctiles que están ganando popularidad entre usuarios con discapacidad visual y que pueden utilizarse, entre otros dispositivos, en cocinas y placas de vitrocerámica.

Stactiles son unas pegatinas con relieve y diferentes texturas diseñadas para proporcionar una referencia táctil sobre superficies que, de otro modo, resultan completamente lisas.

La propuesta de Hable One es sencilla: colocar una pequeña marca táctil sobre el control que se quiere identificar para poder localizarlo mediante el tacto. Las pegatinas incorporan colores de alto contraste y diferentes formas, símbolos o texturas, por lo que pueden servir tanto como referencia visual como táctil.

La compañía dispone de diferentes colecciones, entre ellas conjuntos de formas básicas, símbolos, emojis, letras y Braille.

Uno de los usos que más interés está despertando es su aplicación en los electrodomésticos de cocina .

Las placas de vitrocerámica y otros aparatos modernos utilizan cada vez más paneles de control táctiles. Al desaparecer los botones físicos, una persona con baja visión puede tener dificultades para localizar un determinado control o distinguir entre diferentes funciones.

Las Stactiles permiten colocar referencias táctiles en puntos concretos del panel. Por ejemplo, pueden utilizarse para identificar el botón de encendido, determinadas temperaturas o niveles de potencia, o establecer una referencia que facilite localizar los diferentes controles.

Hable One señala específicamente que sus Stactiles son resistentes al calor y al agua , y las recomienda para marcar controles de hornos, freidoras de aire y lavadoras, entre otros electrodomésticos.

En una vitrocerámica, por ejemplo, una persona podría establecer una referencia táctil que le permita encontrar con mayor facilidad el botón de encendido y, a partir de ahí, orientarse sobre el resto de controles.

Una de las características más interesantes de Stactiles es que no todas las pegatinas tienen el mismo relieve.

La colección de formas básicas incluye símbolos como círculos, cuadrados, triángulos, signos más y menos o chevrones, además de diferentes texturas. De esta forma, no es necesario utilizar siempre el mismo tipo de marca para todos los controles.

Esto puede permitir crear un sistema de referencias personalizado. Por ejemplo, una textura podría utilizarse para identificar el encendido, otra para los controles de aumento y disminución y otra para localizar una función concreta.

La elección y colocación de las marcas dependerá, lógicamente, de las necesidades y preferencias de cada persona.

Su utilidad no se limita a los electrodomésticos.

Hable One ha diseñado Stactiles para poder utilizarse también sobre superficies táctiles , proporcionando un punto físico de referencia sobre interfaces que normalmente no ofrecen ningún tipo de relieve.

Según la información del fabricante, el material permite presionar a través de la propia pegatina para activar el control situado debajo. Esto abre posibilidades interesantes para adaptar diferentes dispositivos electrónicos que utilizan paneles planos y táctiles.

Este planteamiento resulta especialmente interesante porque una de las tendencias actuales en diseño de electrodomésticos y dispositivos electrónicos es precisamente la sustitución de botones físicos por controles táctiles.

La principal ventaja de este tipo de productos es precisamente su sencillez.

No requieren instalar una aplicación ni modificar electrónicamente el electrodoméstico. Se trata de añadir referencias físicas a una interfaz que originalmente no las tiene .

Además, pueden combinarse con otras estrategias de accesibilidad. En una cocina, por ejemplo, una persona puede utilizar referencias táctiles junto con contraste de color, iluminación adecuada y otras técnicas de organización que faciliten la orientación.

No obstante, las Stactiles no convierten por sí solas un electrodoméstico en completamente accesible. Su utilidad dependerá del diseño del aparato, de la distribución de sus controles y de las necesidades visuales y táctiles de cada usuario.

Durante las últimas semanas, las Stactiles han comenzado a aparecer con frecuencia en publicaciones de usuarios con baja visión y ceguera en redes sociales: vídeo

Algunos usuarios están mostrando cómo las utilizan para adaptar electrodomésticos que originalmente carecen de controles físicos, como microondas, lavavajillas o aparatos de cocina.

Este tipo de demostraciones resulta especialmente interesante porque permite ver una aplicación muy práctica de la tiflotecnología: adaptar objetos cotidianos sin necesidad de sustituirlos por productos específicos para personas con discapacidad visual .

Las Stactiles son un buen ejemplo de cómo pequeñas modificaciones pueden marcar una diferencia importante en el día a día.

Frente a dispositivos tecnológicos más complejos, estas pegatinas ofrecen una solución física, económica y relativamente sencilla para introducir referencias táctiles en objetos que hasta ahora podían resultar difíciles de utilizar de forma autónoma.

En el caso de las cocinas, donde la identificación precisa de los controles es especialmente importante, disponer de referencias táctiles puede facilitar la interacción con placas, hornos y otros electrodomésticos.

La aparición de soluciones como Stactiles también pone sobre la mesa una cuestión más amplia: cuando los controles físicos desaparecen, la accesibilidad debe seguir estando presente en el diseño de las interfaces .

Mientras los fabricantes continúan apostando por superficies táctiles y controles cada vez más minimalistas, productos como estas pegatinas muestran una forma sencilla de recuperar parte de la información física que se pierde con ese cambio.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

en.title: Apple Releases tvOS 27
en.summary: Apple has today released tvOS 27 for Apple TV 4K (2nd generation and later). According to Apple , tvOS 27 includes support for larger accessibility text sizes, high-resolution lossless audio in Apple Music, and a redesigned Podcasts app. More details should become available in the near future when Apple updates its "About Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD software updates" Apple Support document. Unfortunately, we were not able to test tvOS 27 during the beta cycle; and thus we do not have any information on whether this release contains any changes to vision accessibility features beyond the added support for larger text sizes. If you have upgraded to tvOS 27, we would greatly appreciate hearing your experiences with the update. To install tvOS 27, go to the Settings channel, then look for the System section near the bottom. From here, look for Software Updates under Maintenance, then select Update Software and Download and Install. Wait for your Apple TV to download the update. Don't disconnect or unplug your Apple TV until the update completes.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
en.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are now available to the public. (Note: As spotted by AppleVis Community Member TJT 2001 , Apple has also released iOS/iPadOS 26.7 for those not wishing to upgrade to iOS 27.) This post contains Apple's Release Notes for iOS 27, as well as links to all of AppleVis' content related to these updates. Also included are instructions on how to install the update. iOS 27 Release Notes iOS 27 introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, as well as new features to help parents create safe digital experiences for kids, and improvements that make iOS more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. The next generation of Apple Intelligence also powers new features across apps that simplify the things you do every day, like editing images in Photos, communicating in Messages and Mail, and browsing in Safari. New parental controls and significant updates to Screen Time make it more intuitive and easy to use, so parents can feel confident that they're building the right digital experience for their child. And with improvements that span design, performance, connectivity, search, and more, the experience on iOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Siri mode in Camera integrates Visual Intelligence into the Camera app, letting you ask questions and take action with what's in front of you, like splitting a bill or looking up nutritional info for a plate of food. Write with Siri enables you to generate a draft from scratch, edit what you've written, or get feedback from Siri virtually anywhere you type. In Messages & Mail, Siri personalizes your writing style based on your relationships, and uses unique phrases and punctuation that you've previously used in your conversations with those people. Apple Intelligence across apps (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Photos. Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the composition of a photo after it was taken by virtually changing the camera position. Extend tool intelligently expands images beyond their edges with realistic infill, so you can straighten horizons, change aspect ratios, or add more space around a subject. Clean Up supports removing even larger objects, with more realistic, high-quality results, and you can choose between Fast mode for small blemishes or High Quality for more intricate edits. Safari. Organize by Topic uses Apple Intelligence to sort your tabs, analyzing webpages and automatically grouping similar tabs together. Notify Me can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability. Describe an Extension lets you create a custom extension using natural language to adjust your view of a website's content or formatting. All-new Image Playground uses a new generative model to make high-quality images in virtually any style, including photorealistic, lets you modify your images using touch and natural language, and lets you generate Lock Screen wallpapers and Contact Posters with personalized suggestions. Describe a Shortcut lets you use natural language to create a shortcut or refine an existing one. Home. Summarized activity notifications combine related alerts across accessories into a single notification. Video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video recordings summarize what's happening in a clip for eligible iCloud+ subscribers. Camera clip search lets you find specific moments from your HomeKit Secure Video cameras by searching in the Home app or Spotlight when on an eligible iCloud+ plan. Describe an event in Calendar lets you use natural language to create an event, and details like the time, location, invitees, and event title are filled in using Apple Intelligence. Suggestions in Mail help you take action based on the context of your emails, like getting directions to a restaurant you booked. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you're speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Accessibility. VoiceOver enhancements include more detailed and contextual image understanding for photos, charts, and screenshots, a conversational experience that lets you ask questions about your screen or surroundings, and a new way to get answers fast with an Action button integration. An enhanced Magnifier experience offers conversational visual assistance for users with low vision, with a high-contrast interface and natural language app controls for zooming and other Magnifier functions. A smarter Accessibility Reader uses intelligence to provide better text cleanup and formatting, images and tables, on-demand summaries, and translation. Voice Control flexible inputs help you navigate your device with just your voice by describing elements on screen in your own words, like "tap the gear" or "tap the button in the top right". And more, including additional ways to create and modify Genmoji, automatic proofreading, and more accurate dictation using an on-device model on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Child Safety Improved setup experience for new child accounts lets parents choose the exact apps their kids can access when they set up an iPhone for their child. Ask to Browse gives parents the option to approve each new website before their child can view it. Expanded Communication Safety protections help intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos. Time Allowances help parents set boundaries around how long kids can use apps across Entertainment, Games, and Social Media apps, offering guidance based on expert research and tailored to each child's age. Schedules let parents choose which apps their kids can access at different points in their day and across weekdays and weekends. Redesigned Screen Time settings give parents at-a-glance information about how their kids use their devices, and controls to adjust access in just a few taps. System Improvements Liquid Glass refinements improve overall readability, and a new slider in Settings lets you personalize its appearance from ultra-clear to fully tinted . Faster performance in experiences across the system, including app launches, new photos loading in your Photos library, and AirDrop transfers. Improved search provides more relevant and comprehensive results in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail. Connectivity Assist enables more seamless transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular networks. And more improvements across apps and experiences, including enhancements to iCloud Shared Albums in Photos, Custom EQ for AirPods, support for perimenopause and menopause in Cycle Tracking in the Health app, and independent volume settings for Alarms and Timers. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/ Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 AppleVis iOS 27 Content AppleVis has the following content available for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Blog Post: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements Blog Post: What's new in Accessibility in iOS 27 for Blind and DeafBlind Users , by Scott Davert Podcast: An Overview of the New VoiceOver and Braille Features in iOS 27 , by Michael Hansen Podcast: A Demonstration of the New Image Description Features in iOS 27 , by David Nason Podcast: A Demonstration and Walk-Through of the New Live Recognition Features in iOS 27 , by Levi Gobin How to Update iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: macOS Golden Gate: New Features, Changes, Improvements, and Bugs for Blind and Low Vision Users
en.summary: Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories . Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with. A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community. Changes for VoiceOver and Braille Users Improved Image and Screen Descriptions As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can. New Verbosity Options for Coding With macOS Golden Gate, you can customize how information such as line numbers, errors, and warnings are reported by VoiceOver in code editors like Xcode. These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings. New "Actions" rotor for trackpad users With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it. "Ducking Amount" setting The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound. Braille Improvements While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, text field labels can now be shown in braille. You can change the format these labels are presented in, or hide them entirely, by going to VoiceOver Utility > Braille > Layout, and clicking Text Field Labels. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, Braille Access in macOS Golden Gate supports plain text (txt) and portable document format (PDF) files. Improvements for Low Vision Users While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvement for low vision users: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, content in Accessibility Reader can now be summarized and translated while retaining its original formatting on macOS Golden Gate. If you are a low vision Mac user, we would love to hear in the comments your experience and thoughts on this and any additional enhancements you encounter in macOS Golden Gate. Other Changes As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the Aaron (English US), Arthur (English UK), Catherine (English Australia), Gordon (English Australia), and Martha (English UK) voices have been reintroduced with macOS Golden Gate. Like other voices, they can be used with Siri, as well as for accessibility functions like VoiceOver and Read & Speak. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, subtitles for spoken dialog in videos where captioning is not already provided can be generated automatically in macOS Golden Gate. These can be turned on and adjusted when playing a video by clicking the "show legible media selection menu" button in the playback controls group. Writing Tools, previously accessed from many apps' Edit menus, as well as many text fields' context menus, is now accessed with VoiceOver by focusing on a text field and choosing "Show Writing Tools" from the Actions Menu. When toggling Cursor Tracking with VO-F3, its state is reflected in the "Mouse pointer:" popup menu in VoiceOver Utility. In prior versions of macOS, the state of Cursor Tracking was not reflected in this popup menu, which had the potential to confuse users. Change List In its support documentation, Apple lists the following changes for VoiceOver users in macOS Golden Gate: You can now turn off announcements that webpages send automatically, such as live scores, new messages, or status updates. Turn off Enable Web Announcements to silence announcements from a single area of a webpage or from the entire page. VoiceOver remembers your choice for that website, so the area stays silent the next time you visit. With the new Coding tab in the Verbosity category of VoiceOver Utility, you can choose whether VoiceOver announces line numbers, and whether it plays a tone or speaks a description when it encounters an error, a breakpoint, or the program counter. Bug Fixes and New Bugs for VoiceOver Users Below are lists of the bugs we believe to have been resolved in macOS Golden Gate, as well as new bugs introduced in this release. We strongly recommend that you read through the list of new bugs and any replies before updating, as this will allow you to make an informed decision on whether to install macOS Golden Gate or wait for a future release. While we are confident in the status of issues contained in this post, we do not claim that our bug list is definitive or that our assessments are infallible. Some issues may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features, and the number of available configurations and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and it is also likely that you will encounter issues that we did not experience during our own testing and daily use of macOS Golden Gate. To ensure the information here is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed macOS Golden Gate. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it's even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they're already aware of the ones listed here. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. Accessibility Bugs Resolved in macOS Golden Gate To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or Braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to macOS Golden Gate. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in macOS Tahoe have been resolved or meaningfully improved in macOS Golden Gate: VoiceOver no longer speaks list items on webpages unreliably. Pauses between sentences are no longer extended when using VoiceOver's "Say All" command. It is once again possible to reply to a message in the Message app by selecting the "Reply" action in the Actions menu. The Actions menu for Messages in the Messages app no longer contains redundant tapback actions. New Bugs for VoiceOver Users in macOS Golden Gate Our testing suggests that the following bugs have been introduced in macOS Golden Gate: After clicking the “Proofread” button in the Writing Tools popover using VoiceOver, only the Next, Previous, and Close buttons are visible, with no way to view the specific changes made to the text. There is no way to open or redownload apps from the “Apps & Purchases” page in the App Store using VoiceOver, with each app conveyed only as a button with no actions available and nothing to interact with besides the app’s name. To redownload a previously purchased app, you must click the [app name] button to open the product page, and then click the "Redownload" button in the toolbar. The sections and buttons in Safari’s Page Menu lack accessibility labels. Interacting with a section and pressing VO-Space on an item (all of which are clearly labeled) works to activate the item; however, interacting with each item in a section reveals an unlabeled button. When playing audio or video, VoiceOver announces “system has new window” once the media has started playing. The identity and purpose of this window is not clear from this announcement, and no new items appear in the application or window chooser menus. Other Possible Bugs In addition to the bugs listed here, we strongly recommend you read this Megathread about the macOS Golden Gate RC , , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software that may differ from our own. macOS Golden Gate release notes macOS 27 introduces Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence, new parental controls, and an expansive set of improvements that make your Mac even more responsive, reliable, and delightful. Experience the new Siri AI Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings. Take action on what’s onscreen With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space. Powerful new ways to edit photos Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex. New tools to browse in Safari Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes. Easily create Shortcuts using natural language With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic. Even more refined design Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design. New child safety features Powerful new parental controls help parents manage what content their children see, who they can communicate with, and when they can access apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage kids’ time in apps across categories. Schedules manage which apps kids can access at different times of day and throughout the week. A more responsive and delightful experience An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable. Learn more Discover even more powerful capabilities in the next release by visiting apple.com/os/macos . For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100 . Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability . Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence . Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and battery life. To learn more, please visit: support.apple.com/125039 . In Conclusion We would like to thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute. We'd love to hear your thoughts after you've had a chance to install the upgrade. What new features do you find most useful? Are there any changes you don't like? Please share your feedback in the comments below. When doing so, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in macOS Golden Gate. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we thank Apple's Accessibility team for their prompt response in fixing many of the bugs reported during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle. However, many longstanding issues remain unresolved, and we find the inability to fully use the Proofread function, a key feature of Apple Intelligence, during a cycle where enhancements to Apple Intelligence were heavily emphasized, incredibly disappointing. We encourage Apple to promptly address this and other outstanding accessibility issues discussed in this post and the comments below so that macOS can be as accessible, usable, and enjoyable as possible for all users. To install macOS Golden Gate, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Upgrade Now button to begin the upgrade process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. More information on how to update the software on your Mac is available on this Apple Support page.

Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories .

Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with.

A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community.

As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can.

These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings.

With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it.

The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound.

Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. A more responsive and delightful experience

An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable.

en.title: watchOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver Features, Issues, and Improvements
en.summary: Apple has today released watchOS 27 to the public. watchOS 27 is compatible with the Apple Watch Series 9 and later and the Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later. Due to the inherent challenges of beta software testing on watchOS, our testing of watchOS 27 has been quite limited. That said, for VoiceOver users, there is at least one new bug that we are aware of and a handful of new features and improvements. New VoiceOver Bugs in watchOS 27 There is rather significant latency with VoiceOver speech when swiping through the user interface. Specifically, there is a delay between when the VoiceOver sound effects/haptics play, and when VoiceOver speaks. Our testing suggests that this issue is not synthesizer-specific. It is unclear to us whether this behavior is simply a function of the newer operating system encountering the limits of hardware (something that has historically been a challenge on Apple Watch devices), or whether this is something that can be resolved by Apple in a future software update. A Feedback report has been filed, and we will keep the community advised as additional information becomes available. If you identify any additional vision accessibility bugs in watchOS 27, please let us know by posting a comment. New VoiceOver Features and Improvements in watchOS 27 There is a new "Tap to Wake" toggle in VoiceOver settings. By default, the setting is enabled, and the Watch will be woken when you tap on the screen. Our best understanding is that disabling this feature should prevent the device from waking when the screen is tapped. It is now possible to customize the speaking of VoiceOver hints in watchOS. Available options are 'Always', 'Never', and 'App-Specific Hints'. On the Clock Face, VoiceOver now speaks the names of Complications before speaking their content. For example, VoiceOver might say, "Weather, Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees," instead of just saying "Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees." For braille display users, there is a new setting, "Translate After a Delay." There are other braille settings that we also believe may be new in this release, but our braille-related testing in watchOS is very limited and so this is not something we are able to comment on with any level of certainty. If you spot any other new features/changes in watchOS 27 or have any corrections to the above, please do let us know by posting a comment. watchOS 27 Release Notes watchOS 27 features the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, updates to Workout Buddy, a new tap gesture, a dynamic app grid to make it easier to access your most used apps, and improvements that make watchOS 27 more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. With improvements that span areas like fitness, design, performance, and more, the experience on watchOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on paired iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Apple Intelligence across apps Workout Buddy delivers motivation with new insights and is now available without your iPhone nearby when you have a Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you’re speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Cycle Tracking Cycle deviation notifications that are suggestive of perimenopause can be received by those age 40 and over. Watch Faces Siri Modular face features a rectangular complication that mirrors the top widget of the Smart Stack, which dynamically updates to show the most relevant widget, as well as a Siri complication to quickly invoke Siri. Smart Stack Single-handed tap gesture enables you to tap your index finger and thumb together once to select a widget in the Smart Stack, even if your other hand is occupied. New suggestion widgets will be surfaced when most relevant to you, including a Parked Car location, birthday reminders for a close contact, balance changes on a transit card, Noise app after a loud noise notification, and more. System Improvements Dynamic app grid highlights your most popular and recently used apps. Find My app is now consolidated into one app to show People, Devices, and Items with a map-centric interface. Media playback now starts faster. Workout app makes distance calculations during treadmill workouts even more accurate from the first step of every walk or run. Fitness app features more accurate route maps after workouts. Battery extension notifications may be proactively offered to disable certain features to increase battery life, including gestures, Start Workout reminders, and Raise to Speak method of invoking Siri. Shazam in the Smart Stack and Music Recognition app identifies songs offline without an internet connection and delivers results automatically when you’re back online. Liquid Glass refinements improve readability with more uniform refraction and improved contrast. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 How to Update watchOS 27 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.
