en.title: Issue Affecting Some JAWS and Fusion Features Now Resolved
en.summary: The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part. Last week a Microsoft update changed the way accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features …
en.body:
The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part.

Last week a Microsoft update changed the way accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features provided no speech or braille. This affected the JAWS Results Viewer, OCR Viewer, Picture Smart, and Message Center, along with New Outlook and Microsoft Copilot 365.

On September 6 we deployed a temporary change to JAWS so that customers would not have to wait while the underlying problem was still being investigated. On September 7 Microsoft released an update that corrected the root cause. Because that update resolves the problem at its source, we have since removed our temporary change.

The Microsoft update is delivered automatically, so there is nothing for you to install or turn on. The temporary work-around we shared last week, toggling the Touch Cursor off and on, is no longer needed.

If you are still experiencing the problem, please restart your computer so the Microsoft update can take effect. If that does not resolve it, please contact your local dealer or our technical support team.

We appreciate everyone who reported this to us and who let us know when things began working again. Those reports helped us confirm the cause quickly and gave us what we needed to work with Microsoft toward a resolution.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 26.6.2 and iPadOS 26.6.2 with Fix for Problems Downloading Updates over Cellular Connections
en.summary: Apple has today released iOS 26.6.2 and iPadOS 26.6.2, bringing a fix for an issue that prevented users from downloading updates over cellular connections. As iOS 26.6.2 and iPadOS 26.6.2 were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a specific issue, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. Release Notes iOS 26.6.2 This update fixes an issue that prevents downloading a software update over a cellular connection. iPadOS 26.6.2 This update fixes an issue that prevents downloading a software update over a cellular connection. How to Update iOS and iPadOS 26.6.2 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: In-Process 8th September 2026
en.summary: It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new: NVDA 2026.2 Magnifier A new Beta already? Resetting to Factory Defaults NVDA 2026.2 NVDA 2026.2 has been released! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.… Read More
en.body:
It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new:

NVDA 2026.2 has been released ! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.

The Magnifier provides zoom and color filtering options to assist users with visual impairments. The Magnifier currently only supports full screen mode, with docked modes planned in a future release. Touch support has been significantly expanded with new pinch gestures and touch-based browse mode navigation for web content. You can now navigate between links, headings, form fields, and other elements using touch flicks.

Speech features have been enhanced with support for custom speech dictionaries that can be provided by add-ons and new dictionary entry types for more granular control. A new voice setting for OneCore voices was added to control pauses after punctuation. A new command allows repeating the last spoken information, with the ability to display it in a browsable message. The default gesture to repeat the last spoken information is NVDA+x , which can be changed in the Input Gestures dialog.

The braille display can now automatically scroll, and DotPad devices support multi-button combinations. The default gesture to toggle automatic scroll is NVDA+alt+k .

Liblouis has been updated with new Italian and Estonian braille tables. When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration.

Download the new version from the NVDA 2026.2 release post (or by checking for updates from within NVDA).

As well as the article below, and a new extensive section on the magnifier in the User Guide, our “Basic Training for NVDA” module has been updated with a number of updates. Of particular interest is a new section on the magnifier, there is also a topic covering reading the last spoken information and other new and improved content. These new updates are currently only available in the electronic text version. You can purchase Basic Training for NVDA from our shop . If you have already purchased the module, you can download the new version with the Magnifier section from the downloads page after logging into your NV Access account .

We are very excited to incorporate a magnifier into NVDA for the first time. We have had a lot of comments from users who are excited for this feature, and we’ve had some questions too, so let’s cover off some of the things it can and cannot do, and why it is a useful addition to NVDA:

First Release Firstly, it’s worth highlighting that this is the first release of NVDA with a magnifier and so the features will improve over time. We try to ship NVDA features incrementally, keeping the initial design scope small and allowing for early user feedback. This allows us to grow the magnifier in response to user reaction. Currently NVDA only works as a full-screen magnifier. We plan to extend the options in future releases. Adding windowed / docked modes is a high priority once bugs are addressed and the full-screen mode is more polished.

What CAN the magnifier do? The magnifier has most of the features you might expect from such a feature: You can zoom in and out (from 1x up to 50x) The view will follow the mouse, keyboard focus, browse mode focus and NVDA navigator object and review cursor – user selectable You can pan the view with the keyboard, in configurable increments, or jump to the edges of the screen You can adjust the colours (normal, inverted or greyscale) You can choose how objects are tracked (Centred or relative to their position on screen) You can configure the keystrokes for the various functions There is a keystroke to briefly zoom out and show an overview of the screen

We have made a short demo of the magnification feature on our YouTube channel .

Should I change magnifiers? Particularly if you currently use another magnification solution, we very much encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier. We are interested in your feedback, and particularly where you would like to see our feature improve.

If you already use Windows magnifier or another program, you can keep using it and it will continue to work with NVDA’s speech functions. Just as we don’t recommend having two screen readers running at once, we also wouldn’t recommend having NVDA’s magnifier AND another magnifier running at the same time.

If you do currently use Windows Magnifier, some of the reasons you may consider NVDA’s magnifier: It starts when NVDA starts (once you enable it) Configurable keystrokes Greyscale colour filtering mode Relative tracking mode Ability to follow NVDA’s object navigation and review cursor Keys to jump to edges of screen No settings window always on screen Ability to set your desired settings once and save to a portable copy you can use on any computer

If you use Windows magnifier in docked or lens mode, or some of the other features which haven’t yet made it into the NVDA magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, then you may wish to stay with Windows magnifier for now – but we do encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier and let us know what you think.

Before we even got this edition of In-Process finished, to tell you all about 2026.2…. we ALREADY have a new beta? Of NVDA 2026.3 ? Yep! And I’m not going to talk about that yet – if you want to check it out, please head to the beta release announcement . What I did want to briefly mention, was how we came to have a new beta out, when the paint isn’t even dry on NVDA 2026.2?

Great question! And it comes down to how we develop software. Both our internal developers, and the community are constantly working on improving features, fixing bugs, and adding new things into NVDA. As a new piece of code gets incorporated into NVDA, it goes into an “Alpha” build – an early pre-release build with whatever has been changed recently. This lets our developers and our most dedicated testers try it out and give feedback. These come out almost daily (and sometimes several in one day). Because of the quick turnaround, we don’t share them on social media or here on the blog, but if you’d like to try them out, alpha builds are publicly available from the snapshots page . Be aware that they may not be as polished as the stable releases – though the process to test them out is identical.

So, generally a week after a stable release, we collate all the things which have been in alpha for at least a couple of weeks, and put them together into a “beta” release of the next version. While we may still have some features we are working on for later betas, as well any regressions or major issues discovered from the previous release, we can turn much of our development attention on towards the NEXT release.

So, if you ever find an issue with NVDA, the sooner you let us know, the sooner we can prioritise it and work on a fix as needed.

One of the perhaps less glamourous updates in NVDA 2026.2 is to a feature you hopefully don’t ever need to use.

“When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration”

We’ve covered resetting NVDA to factory defaults previously , though it is worth being aware of. While something you hopefully don’t need, if you ever DO need it, it’s good to know it exists. With this new change, if you reset NVDA to factory defaults, a dialog appears advising “Your configuration has been reset to factory defaults. Choose OK to keep factory defaults, or Undo to restore your previous configuration”. This could be useful just in case you ever inadvertently activate the wrong item on the NVDA menu for instance, and may hopefully save you from needing go through setting up NVDA to your preferences again.

That’s all for this week, do update to NVDA 2026.2 if you haven’t already, and we’d love to hear your feedback on the new features – the magnifier of course, but also the other updates.

Muy atentos: Después de casi dos años de desarrollo, por fin llega TCA ConvertDoc 1.5. No es una simple actualización: es un salto generacional con las funcionalidades que me habéis ido pidiendo en los comentarios del blog, sobre todo desde la entrada de la versión 1.4. Para quienes aún no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA ConvertDoc? TCA ConvertDoc es una pequeña utilidad portable y gratuita para Windows, con interfaz 100% accesible y atajos de teclado, que nos permite convertir entre multitud de formatos de documentos (doc, docx, RTF, epub, pdf, HTML, odt, txt, markdown, PNG, JPG, PPTx), hacer OCR a imágenes y PDFs, y ahora, además, traducir. Y todo, de forma individual o por lotes (carpeta entera de una sola vez). Pues bien, la 1.5 llega cargada de novedades. Os las cuento todas. Novedades de TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 1. Conversión DOCX → PDF (individual y por lotes) Ahora podéis convertir documentos de Word a PDF con un solo clic. ¿Tenéis una carpeta llena de? docx? La conversión masiva procesa todo el directorio de golpe, manteniendo el formato, las imágenes y la estructura del documento. Perfecto para preparar entregas, archivar o compartir. 2. Conversión PPTX → Markdown (individual y por lotes) Algunos me preguntasteis en la entrada de la 1.4 por qué ciertas presentaciones de PowerPoint no se pueden leer con lectores de pantalla. Pues esta es una de las soluciones: extrae el contenido de tus presentaciones a Markdown limpio y editable, ideal para documentación, blogs, wikis o migrar contenido. También funciona en lote para carpetas completas. 3. PDF escaneado PDF buscable (OCR) "¿Se puede convertir un pdf en un pdf con capacidad de búsqueda?" — me preguntasteis en los comentarios de la 1.4. ¡Ahora sí! Añades un PDF que es solo imagen (un escaneo sin capa de texto), TCA ConvertDoc le aplica OCR y te devuelve un PDF con texto seleccionable y buscable. Accesibilidad real para documentos heredados, del tipo que sea. 4. JPG / PNG PDF buscable Construye PDFs accesibles a partir de imágenes sueltas. Cada imagen pasa por OCR y se une en un único PDF donde puedes buscar, copiar y seleccionar el texto. Ideal para digitalizar notas, facturas, páginas de libros o documentos fotografiados con el móvil. 5. Traducción integrada! (¡la gran novedad!) Llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo incorporarle la traducción a TCA ConvertDoc, y por fin está aquí. Ahora el programa es capaz de traducir archivos completos a cualquier idioma usando dos motores: • Argos Translate | Offline | Descarga previa de los paquetes de idioma (privacidad total, sin internet) • Google Translate | Online | Conexión a internet, máxima calidad Formatos soportados: .txt, .docx y .pdf. Y lo mejor de todo: traduce incluso archivos grandes como libros enteros. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Nada de copiar y pegar por trozos, ni de chocar con límites ridículos de caracteres. Un detalle importante sobre Argos: la primera vez que uses Argos con un idioma, te aparecerá un diálogo ofreciéndote descargar los paquetes de ese idioma... y solo esa única vez. A partir de ahí, ese idioma queda instalado en el programa y funciona totalmente sin conexión. Tranquilo, no te lo volverá a pedir. 6. Selector de idiomas del OCR (Tesseract) completo En la 1.4 teníamos 3 idiomas de OCR (español, inglés e italiano). Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo. 7. Arreglos y optimizaciones internas OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz. Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes. Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas. Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas. Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido. Requisitos para utilizar TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: • Windows10 (x64) en adelante. • portable, sin instalación. • Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline • Para Google Translate: conexión a internet Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión. Tutorial: 📘 TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: OCR en PDF, 🚀 traduce libros y más! En este tutorial les mostraré: • Les mostraré la nueva conversión de Docx a PDF. • Conversión de PPTX a Markdown. • Conversión de un PDF (que son imágenes) a un PDF accesible (que admite búsqueda). • Construir un archivo PDF a partir de imágenes Jpg o PNG. • Muestra de que todos los idiomas ahora se cargan en el Motor OCR Tesseract. • Como traducir un documento en formato TXT a otro idioma de forma Online usando Google Translate (• conversión del inglés al español). • Como traducir un documento en formato Docx, utilizando la traducción OfLine con Argos Translate (• muestra del inglés al francés, descarga de idiomas y más). • Finalmente les mostraré, como traducir un PDF a otro idioma. La descarga. Les dejaré en la descarga: • El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial). • El programa TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 x64. • Archivo con las librerías visual estudio C++. Espero les sea de mucha utilidad: Dos años son mucho tiempo en software, pero TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 llega para quedarse. No es un parche: es un salto que cubre el ciclo completo —convertir, OCR, buscar, traducir— en una sola herramienta accesible, portable, gratuita y sin suscripciones. Si trabajas con documentos, investigas, digitalizas archivo o necesitas mover contenido entre idiomas, esta versión te va a ahorrar horas. Y la traducción de libros enteros, esa que tanto esperabais, por fin es una realidad. ¿Qué funcionalidad echabas más en falta? ¿Se te ocurre algo para la 1?6? Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes.

Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas.

Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas.

Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido.

• portable, sin instalación.

• Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline

Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión.

En este tutorial les mostraré:

Les dejaré en la descarga:

es.title: Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 288e684536edb011710d760fc18ba7b652241085742e304e17d8ee01ede2d20f. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

This may affect: The issue is not currently observed in web browsers such …
en.body:
A recent Microsoft update is changing how accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS may not receive the information it needs from these applications, causing some features to provide no speech or braille.

This may affect:

The issue is not currently observed in web browsers such as Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.

If you find that JAWS is not working as expected in web-based apps, toggle the Touch Cursor on and off again for JAWS to resume speaking normally. To enable the Touch Cursor, press SHIFT+NUM PAD PLUS if using Desktop keyboard layout and CAPS LOCK+SHIFT+SEMICOLON if using Laptop keyboard layout. To toggle it off and return to the Virtual PC Cursor, press NUM PAD PLUS twice quickly (in Desktop layout) or hold CAPS LOCK and press SEMICOLON twice quickly in Laptop layout.

If the content still does not respond as expected, press F5 to refresh the page or application content.

Vispero is working directly with Microsoft to investigate the issue and determine the appropriate fix. We will provide additional information when it becomes available.

es.body:
¡Hola, comunidad! ¿Cómo han ido estos meses de descanso? Esperamos que hayan servido para cargar las pilas y empezar este nuevo año lectivo con energía. Nosotros, aunque no hemos desconectado del todo para informarte de la llegada de NVDA 2026.2 y actualizar traducciones, estamos listos para seguir adelante con nuestra actividad habitual. Si recuerdas el anuncio de la beta 7 de NVDA 2026.2 , vino acompañado de una mala noticia: el fallecimiento de Rui Fontes, miembro muy activo de la comunidad a nivel internacional y propietario de Tiflotecnia, la compañía que actualmente comercializa las voces más recientes de Vocalizer para NVDA. Tras este triste anuncio, la venta de las voces quedó en pausa, a la espera de que se aclarase la situación en Tiflotecnia. Desde NVDA.es nos complace anunciar que dicha aclaración ya ha tenido lugar, y por tanto volvemos a reactivar la venta de este sintetizador de voz rápido y de alta calidad. En consecuencia, ya puedes volver a adquirir licencias completas por 90 euros, y actualizaciones de licencias de la versión 3 a la 4 por 50 euros, en ambos casos con impuestos incluidos. Recuerda que cada licencia te permitirá usar el sintetizador en hasta tres equipos de forma simultánea. Si vas a formatear o quieres hacer cambios relevantes de hardware, puedes devolver tu licencia al servidor para recuperarla más adelante. Además, es posible activar y desactivar licencias en equipos que no disponen de conexión a Internet, algo que con la versión 3.0 no se podía hacer. Y por si fuera poco, una sola licencia incluye todas las voces disponibles, ¡en todos los idiomas y con todas las calidades! Si todavía no lo has hecho, puedes instalar y probar estas voces sin coste alguno durante una semana. Te animamos a hacerlo, ¡la experiencia merece la pena! ¡Hasta la próxima!

La entrada Regresan las voces Tiflotecnia a la tienda de NVDA en español se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

blindGram is an independent accessible Telegram client for blind and low-vision Android users, based on Telegram’s open-source Android code.

Its optional blindGram Assistant reads text inside images, provides offline image labels, and converts voice messages and round videos to text offline in 23 languages without Telegram Premium.

Optional AI features provide detailed image descriptions, summaries, follow-up questions, and questions about any message through the user’s own OpenRouter, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or compatible provider. AI features remain off until enabled.

Website: https://en.blindgram.ir/

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Designed specifically for blind and low-vision users . Interface and message actions are optimized for screen-reader navigation, with primary testing using TalkBack .

Assistant results open in accessible dialogs or conversation screens where text can be read, selected, and copied.

Offline OCR , image labels, and voice-to-text require no account or Telegram Premium.

AI features are optional and clearly disclose when content leaves the device.

BlindGram 15.0; Supports Android 5.0 and newer;

es.title: Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2
es.summary: Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de magnificador integrado, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y una ampliación de funciones de voz y braille. El magnificador ofrece opciones de aumentos y de filtrado de colores para ayudar a los usuarios con discapacidad visual. Actualmente, el Magnificador solo es compatible con el modo a pantalla completa, aunque en una futura actualización se prevé la incorporación de modos acoplados. Se ha ampliado considerablemente la compatibilidad táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizco y la navegación por el contenido web mediante el modo táctil. Ahora puedes desplazarte entre enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos mediante gestos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con la compatibilidad con diccionarios de voz personalizados que pueden proporcionarse mediante complementos, así como con nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que permiten un control más preciso. Se ha añadido una nueva configuración de voz para las voces de OneCore con el fin de controlar las pausas tras los signos de puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la posibilidad de mostrarla en un mensaje que se pueda leer. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información leída en voz alta es NVDA+x, que se puede modificar en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Ahora, la pantalla braille puede desplazarse automáticamente y los dispositivos DotPad admiten combinaciones de varios botones. El atajo predeterminado para activar o desactivar el desplazamiento automático es NVDA+Alt+k. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas de braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer las opciones predeterminadas de fábrica de NVDA, ahora hay disponible un botón «Deshacer» para recuperar la configuración anterior. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.2, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.2, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es f3f8d29974a88d687b3c4809be192219ec579c5bdabcda5aaf53635288bca824. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc2, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

Why Web Accessibility Matters Web …
en.body:
Web Accessibility In Mind (WebAIM) is surveying screen reader users to collect information that will impact the future development of web content and web standards. WebAIM, part of Utah State University, provides training, tools, and information to assist in the creation of websites that are accessible to individuals with disabilities.

Web accessibility is crucial to ensure screen reader users can readily access information on the web. This includes content such as:

Websites are often used to shop online, complete school assignments, and perform essential work tasks. This makes accessibility a necessary part of website development.

Whether you consider yourself a novice or an advanced JAWS user, we ask that you contribute to the future of web accessibility by taking the WebAIM Screen Reader Survey . It will remain open through Monday, August 31, 2026 , and takes around five to ten minutes to complete.

en.title: AppleVis Unlimited: What's New and Noteworthy for August 2026
en.summary: Welcome to the August 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form. New Apps AudioReel From the App Store: Ever had an audio clip you wanted to post on social media, but couldn't because it's just an audio file? AudioReel solves exactly that: it takes your audio and photos and turns them into a finished video. es.title: Ya disponible la segunda candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la rc 2 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access. A menos … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la segunda candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la segunda candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 2 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.2. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de ampliación, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y capacidades mejoradas de voz y braille. El ampliador proporciona opciones de zoom y filtro de color para asistir a usuarios con baja visión. Actualmente, el ampliador sólo soporta el modo a pantalla completa, dejando los modos acoplados planificados para una futura versión. Se ha expandido significativamente el soporte táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizcar y con navegación en modo exploración táctil en contenido web. Ahora se puede navegar por enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos usando deslizamientos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con soporte de diccionarios del habla personalizados que pueden proporcionarse en complementos y nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que proporcionan un control más granular. Se ha añadido una nueva opción en las voces OneCore para controlar las pausas después de la puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la capacidad de mostrarla en un mensaje explorable. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información verbalizada es NVDA+x, y se puede cambiar desde el diálogo Gestos de entrada. La pantalla braille ahora puede desplazarse automáticamente, y los dispositivos DotPad soportan combinaciones multibotón. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer NVDA a los valores de fábrica, ahora hay disponible un botón de deshacer para restaurar la configuración anterior. Para instalar esta candidata a liberación, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.2 rc 2 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 3e956809bf8ea2812ceb26748d7d49cf869b1023fb8ce94d99589e20af1d7ba1. ¡Feliz miércoles!

La entrada Ya disponible la segunda candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.body:
Welcome to JAWS Jumpstart, a four-week series designed to help students, teachers, new users, and anyone looking for a refresher get the most out of JAWS as the new school year begins. Each Monday in August, we’ll share a practical tip, shortcut, or feature to help you start the year off on the right foot. This week, we’re sharing JAWS customization tips to help you improve productivity and efficiency.

Customizing JAWS enables you to tailor specific settings like speech rate, verbosity, and punctuation to meet your needs. Customization also helps you optimize JAWS for specific applications or tasks, improving efficiency and productivity in your daily work or studies. Here are three tips for customizing JAWS.

Customizing speech settings is important because it ensures JAWS communicates information in a way that is clear, comfortable, and easy for you to understand. To customize speech settings:

PlaceMarkers in JAWS let you mark specific spots on web pages, documents, or emails so you can quickly return to them later. Temporary PlaceMarkers are for one-time use during your current session, while permanent PlaceMarkers are saved and available whenever you revisit the page or document. PlaceMarkers are helpful for navigating long or complex content, making it easier to find important information or start and end text selections.

To create a PlaceMarker:

To return to a PlaceMarker, use CTRL+SHIFT+K to open the PlaceMarkers List and select the marker you want. You can also press K to navigate to PlaceMarkers on a web page.

Using PlaceMarkers helps you efficiently navigate and manage information in large documents or web pages.

You can now save your JAWS settings to the cloud and access them on any computer where you sign in with your Vispero account. This makes it much easier to keep your setup consistent without having to reconfigure JAWS each time. This also ensures your customizations remain safely stored and in situations where your current computer becomes unusable.

With Cloud Settings, you can sync:

These settings will be saved to the cloud so you can sync them on multiple computers. This also makes it easier to restore your settings on a new device.

This feature is only available in regions where Vispero accounts are supported. This feature is also a part of our Early Adopter Program, so you can try it out and provide feedback before it is fully released.

To enable it in the Early Adopter Program and sync your settings:

To learn more about PlaceMarkers or additional ways to customize your JAWS settings, watch or download these archived trainings:

Try these customization tips to improve productivity and enhance the way you work. Have questions? Send an email to training@vispero.com .

en.summary: We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around: NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! Automatically Scrolling the Braille Display Getting help from others New Unassigned Commands Finding out more about what is new NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all… Read More
en.body:
We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around:

The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all users to download this RC and provide feedback. Unless any critical bugs are found, this will be identical to the final 2026.2 release.

NVDA 2026.2 includes:

Magnifier (full screen, colour filtering, zoom, focus tracking) Improved touch gestures (links, form fields, etc) NVDA+x to repeat last spoken information Improved speech dictionaries Automatic Braille Display scrolling & much more!

We would encourage you to try out the NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate , especially if you haven’t yet tried any of the betas. You can do this by creating a portable copy or by selecting “Continue running” from the launcher, to run a temporary copy and not interfere with your installed copy of NVDA.

One of the new features in NVDA 2026.2, is that we: “Added the ability to automatically scroll the braille display”. This comes courtesy of Noelia, one of our prominent Spanish contributors. Reading the user guide entry for the new “Automatic scroll rate” feature, it notes:

Automatic braille scrolling can be enabled to scroll the display at a set speed. When using this feature, the braille display scrolls to present information which is more than will fit on the display at once. The feature is disabled by default. You can change the gestures assigned to use automatic braille scrolling in NVDA’s Input Gestures dialog before it can be used. Gestures are also available to speed up or slow down the rate of automatic scrolling. Alternatively, you can set the automatic scroll rate in Braille Settings.

While braille is scrolling, you can still use the scroll back and scroll forward commands without stopping scrolling. Scroll back can be useful to read previous contents again. Scroll forward can be useful to skip a blank line, or if the line being read is short.

While reading, automatic braille scrolling will stop when any of the following happen:

The toggle automatic braille scrolling key is pressed The user presses a key or gesture which would display a new message The focus is moved (including with braille display panning keys) The end of the document is reached The state of the lock or secure screen is changed (such as the computer being locked)

The commands for this feature are: Toggle automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+k Increase automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+L Decrease automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+j

Last fortnight, we covered ways you can get help from within NVDA itself. This time around, let’s have a look at some of the places you can get help from others. As with last fortnight’s post, this list covers getting help for NVDA itself only, aimed at end users: NV Access Telephone Support : If you’ve still got questions after following last fortnight’s tips and reading Basic Training for NVDA etc, give us a call. Telephone support IS a paid service, and for end-user support only, but it is available 24/7. We have numbers you can call in Australia or the USA, OR you can email us and we can call you anywhere in the world. You also get telephone support included with the NVDA Productivity Bundle . Official NVDA Email Group : While we monitor various other groups, the one place you know you will find NV Access staff, and users, is the official, friendly, NVDA email group at https://nvaccess.org/nvda-users – plus, as a free, welcoming and popular resource, you will often get help from other users even quicker than we can respond. Local language email groups : We have a huge list of email groups in many languages. Know of a group which isn’t listed? Please, let us know so we can share it on the connect page for others! Social media : Our community on Mastodon is the most active, but you can also find us on Facebook and other platforms . NVDA Remote Access : Have a friend who can help with your PC? You can let them connect to your PC to help you. Note there are a number of security measures in place to ensure this feature can only be accessed by deliberate action from both parties.

For the upcoming NVDA 2026.2, we’ve added a couple of new “unassigned” commands. These aren’t always the most obvious to find, so I thought it was worth highlighting them here: Added an unassigned command to toggle keyboard layout. ( #19211 , @CyrilleB79 ) Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z ) Added an unassigned command to report the current status of the Screen Curtain. ( #19759 )

Commands like these can provide useful functionality, but may often only be required by some users. As we are all aware, screen readers already have a lot of keystrokes, so we always have to think carefully before assigning new keystrokes.

For instance, the toggle keyboard layout setting. Most users will setup the keyboard layout how they prefer, and never need to change it. For the rare time you may wish to change it, the setting is on the keyboard settings page, which is available with NVDA+control+k . For testing or teaching, a command to toggle the layout on the fly may be invaluable, so, in NVDA 2026.2, it’s there if you need it.

In any NVDA release announcement , there is a link to “ What’s new in this release of NVDA ” (I’ve linked to those to things for NVDA 2026.2 RC1). That document gives a summary of the highlights in several paragraphs, and then bullet points for all the changes in groups: Important notes : information such as older Windows versions no longer supported Security fixes : Updates to NVDA which fix potential security issues. New features : New functionality in NVDA. For instance, NVDA+x to repeat the last spoken information, or the ability to automatically scroll the braille display Changes : Features which may be slightly different, such as renaming the “COM Registration Fixing Tool” to “System Accessibility Repair Tool”. Bug fixes : Fixing features which didn’t work the way they should. For instance, in NVDA 2026.2, we’ve fixed a crash in the add-on store, NVDA now recovers quicker from freezes in some applications, and form controls are correctly reported in Firefox again. Changes for developers : Updates which may affect how contributors code for NVDA. These don’t affect end users directly. For instance, updating the version of Python used, or new functions developers can call to find out information. Deprecations : Again, only for developers, function calls which either no longer work, or have been changed to something else, and developers should transition over to the new function call.

In most of the bullet points for each release, there is a number at the end, and sometimes a username. For instance, in the unassigned commands article above: “Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z )”

In this case, #17005 is the issue number assigned to the original request for this feature. @tareh7z is the GitHub user who wrote the code and submitted the pull request to fix it – thanks @tareh7z! And thanks to ALL our contributors. NVDA 2026.2 is a big release with a lot of amazing features the community have put a lot of work into!

The line in the changes document will hopefully give enough information to quickly describe the feature for most users. The user guide will also have been updated with any relevant information. In this case, look at section 6.1.3 “Other Navigation Commands”, which talks about not only sliders, but other quick navigation commands which don’t have default keystrokes.

The issue number is a link back to that issue, which can be helpful if you’d like to look back at the conversation which prompted the new feature. For instance, in this case, there was some discussion around what other types of information could potentially be accessed with a “slider” command (others that were suggested were ruled out in this case).

That’s all for this time. Do please try out the NVDA 2026.2 release candidate , and of course, let us know of any issues you encounter with it. Next time around we will have more on NVDA 2026.2!

es.title: Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access. A menos … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.2. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de ampliación, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y capacidades mejoradas de voz y braille. El ampliador proporciona opciones de zoom y filtro de color para asistir a usuarios con baja visión. Actualmente, el ampliador sólo soporta el modo a pantalla completa, dejando los modos acoplados planificados para una futura versión. Se ha expandido significativamente el soporte táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizcar y con navegación en modo exploración táctil en contenido web. Ahora se puede navegar por enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos usando deslizamientos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con soporte de diccionarios del habla personalizados que pueden proporcionarse en complementos y nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que proporcionan un control más granular. Se ha añadido una nueva opción en las voces OneCore para controlar las pausas después de la puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la capacidad de mostrarla en un mensaje explorable. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información verbalizada es NVDA+x, y se puede cambiar desde el diálogo Gestos de entrada. La pantalla braille ahora puede desplazarse automáticamente, y los dispositivos DotPad soportan combinaciones multibotón. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer NVDA a los valores de fábrica, ahora hay disponible un botón de deshacer para restaurar la configuración anterior. Para instalar esta candidata a liberación, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.2 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 09dfba7e03f37598a50e8495370a063864acd4de48ce6ebdf9ee320c536803f5. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: A Comprehensive Guide to the Smart Typer Pro App
en.summary: Smart Typer Pro is an all-in-one productivity app for Android devices that completely redefines mobile note-taking, text editing, voice dictation, artificial intelligence assistance, and document…
en.body:
Published 15 August 2026 by Syed Sharib Ali

Smart Typer Pro is an all-in-one productivity app for Android devices that completely redefines mobile note-taking, text editing, voice dictation, artificial intelligence assistance, and document management. Rather than operating as a basic text editor or a single simple tool, Smart Typer Pro serves as a central, easy-to-use digital workspace designed for everyone—from everyday users, students, and writers to content creators and users who rely on accessibility features.

This comprehensive guide breaks down every single feature, setting, handy customization, system integration, and daily shortcut inside Smart Typer Pro in clear, easy-to-understand detail.

Download the app on Google Play

Table of Contents

Smart Typer Pro keeps all your work neat, organized, and easy to find on your Android phone or tablet. When you open the app, it automatically creates a main folder named Smart Typer directly in your device’s main internal storage root ( /sdcard/Smart Typer ).

Located at the bottom-right corner of the main screen, the Plus (+) / Create button lets you create new items instantly:

Located at the top-right of the main screen:

By default, long-pressing (holding down) any file or folder brings up a comprehensive context menu loaded with quick actions tailored specifically to the file type:

When you turn on multi-select mode (or select multi-file options), you can handle several items together:

The built-in editor screen is the heart of Smart Typer Pro. It handles everything from quick daily scratch notes to large document files smoothly.

Smart Typer Pro makes typing hands-free easy with voice dictation built straight into the text editor.

Set up custom shorthand phrases in Settings. For example:

While you speak, Smart Typer Pro automatically detects your custom shortcuts and expands them into full sentences instantly.

Smart Typer Pro offers four writing assistant options to refine your notes according to your needs:

The AI Typing Assistant screen offers a dedicated, distraction-free space for dictating text, polishing ideas with AI, and sharing messages directly.

Available from the main menu side drawer and directly from the text editor’s More Options menu, the Quick AI Assistant gives you a friendly, helpful AI chat companion ready to answer questions or help write content.

The Text-to-Handwriting feature turns your digital text notes into realistic handwritten PDF files or image pages.

Smart Typer Pro uses high-quality realistic voice technology to convert your text documents into clear, natural-sounding MP3 audio files. Conveniently access this feature directly from the long-press file context menu ( Convert to Audio ) as well as from the Smart Utilities Hub.

Smart Typer Pro includes built-in pop-up media players so you can listen to audio recordings or watch video clips without needing separate apps.

The Media Scanner tool quickly scans your phone to organize and show all your media files in one clean dashboard.

The Instant Translator tool offers fast, multi-language document translation. Access it conveniently from the Smart Utilities Hub , the long-press file context menu ( Translate Text ), or directly inside the text editor’s More Options menu while working on a note.

The Wikipedia Search tool lets you research topics and extract information right inside the app. Access it from the Smart Utilities Hub or directly while editing notes via the text editor’s More Options menu.

Word Helper uses AI to turn any word or phrase into a comprehensive, easy-to-understand dictionary guide. Access it from the Smart Utilities Hub or directly while writing notes via the text editor’s More Options menu.

The Smart Utilities Hub acts as a central control panel holding all 12 main tools of Smart Typer Pro (including Instant Language Translator, Wikipedia Search, Quick AI Assistant, Word Helper, and Text-to-Audio).

The Settings screen gives you full control over how Smart Typer Pro works:

en.title: Smart Typer Pro
en.summary: Smart Typer is a lightweight yet feature-rich Android productivity application designed to bring notes, file management, advanced text editing, AI tools, and everyday utilities into…
en.body:
Published 14 August 2026 by Syed Sharib Ali

Smart Typer is a lightweight yet feature-rich Android productivity application designed to bring notes, file management, advanced text editing, AI tools, and everyday utilities into a single workspace. It allows users to create, edit, organize, copy, move, rename, share, and convert files while also providing an integrated file manager for browsing and managing device storage.

Its powerful text editor supports both regular writing and coding, with features such as Find & Replace, precise text splitting, multi-selection, voice typing, offline voice-input correction, Markdown/blog writing, and multiple AI-powered text refinement modes. Users can also translate text, look up words with Word Helper, search and read Wikipedia articles, and convert text into PDF, realistic handwriting, or natural-sounding audio.

Smart Typer also includes an AI Companion for answering questions with beautifully formatted responses, an AI Typing Assistant, Archive Viewer for ZIP/RAR files, image, audio, video, and Markdown viewers, and enhanced Microsoft Word document support. With extensive customization, tablet and landscape support, and compatibility with numerous text and document formats, Smart Typer aims to provide a versatile productivity environment for students, writers, developers, professionals, and everyday Android users.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The UI is designed with accessibility in mind and works with prominent Android screen readers, including TalkBack, CSR, and PSR. Interactive buttons and controls are properly labelled, and accessibility actions are provided where applicable, including for file and folder operations. Screen-reader navigation is supported throughout the app, with particular attention given to accessible text editing, file management, and utility workflows. No significant unlabeled-button or accessibility issues are currently known.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

1.4. Android 15

en.summary: Unboxr is the ultimate lightweight and secure tool for extracting archives on your Android device. Designed with a beautiful, modern dark theme using Jetpack Compose,…
en.body:
Published 9 August 2026 by Warren Carr

Unboxr is the ultimate lightweight and secure tool for extracting archives on your Android device. Designed with a beautiful, modern dark theme using Jetpack Compose, Unboxr makes managing compressed files fast and intuitive.

Key Features:

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

“Unboxr” is a simplistic app intended for extracting compressed files, with support for several formats, including password-protected archives.

The UI is straightforward, with an “Open Folder” button that, when tapped, takes you to your phone’s internal storage, where you can choose the location containing the file you want to extract. The app also appears among the apps that can handle these file types, so you can select supported files from a file manager without using the dedicated button in the app.

In the top-right corner, there is a “Settings” button where you can customize the app. The customization options are quite limited, though. The Settings section also includes a donation option at the very bottom of the screen labeled “Buy me a coffee”

The app is completely free and contains no ads.

The app is very minimalistic. I noticed that it is not possible to make the app ask you where you want the contents to be saved every time you extract a file, despite the presence of an “Always ask” option in Settings, which, based on its explanation, should enable this behavior. Instead, to select the output directory, you have to specify it through the “Default destination folder” option.

When it comes to accessibility, I didn’t encounter any issues with the app.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

v1.0. Android 16

en.title: In-Process 7th August 2026
en.summary: We’re getting ever closer to NVDA 2026.2 and we hit a new milestone towards that this week. Let’s have a look at what’s in this week’s blog and then dive in: NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 Getting Help WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey Thanks Acapela Moving by Sentence NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 NVDA 2026.2 is nearly… Read More
en.body:
We’re getting ever closer to NVDA 2026.2 and we hit a new milestone towards that this week. Let’s have a look at what’s in this week’s blog and then dive in:

NVDA 2026.2 is nearly here! This week we’re up to NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 . We are now in the “String freeze” – that is, we don’t make any changes for a couple of weeks to give the translators time to update their work before the stable release. So, the next step should be a release candidate in a couple of weeks. Then, all going to plan, the final release a week or so after that. Let’s have a look at the updates from the betas since the last In-Process:

Changes introduced in NVDA 2026.2 Beta 10 : Updates to translations Fixed touchscreen, touchpad and mouse input for magnifier Added gestures for braille automatic scroll commands Removed True Center Mode and Border Mode from the magnifier due to design bugs Remove non-functional “Custom” option from the math decimal separator setting

Changes introduced in Beta 9: Updates to translations Update Braille Reading and Automatic Scroll Rate in User Guide Moving by sentence in Word (alt+downArrow/alt+upArrow) at the start/end of a document now stops there instead of wrapping around to the opposite end Changed quick access keys for magnifier settings to ensure they are unique Changes introduced in Beta 8: Updates to translations Improve magnifier behaviour when using higher DPI scaling Fix magnifier from interfering with opening dictionary dialogs Improve the handling of failing to activate the magnifier Block touch screen input when using the magnifier where possible, as it is not supported yet

We try to ensure there are plenty of ways for NVDA users to get help. Since you’re reading this blog post, I HOPE you would consider our blog one of the ways you learn more about NVDA. We have training material and telephone support in our shop, and they are both very popular options (particularly combined in the NVDA Productivity Bundle ). But what about in NVDA itself? There are a couple of ways you can get help while you are using NVDA: The User Guide. (And particularly the quick start guide for new users). The user guide contains information on all of the features of NVDA. It is an excellent resource to refer back to after completing “ Basic Training for NVDA ” and learning about all the features. Press NVDA+n to open the NVDA menu, then h for the help submenu, which starts on the User Guide The other items in the “Help” menu for information including what is new , links to the NV Access website , help and training , and the “ Commands quick reference ” (the tables of keystrokes and gestures extracted from the user guide). Context sensitive help. From within any dialog in NVDA, press f1 to open the user guide to the topic on the current control. Input Help. Press NVDA+1 (the 1 in the number row, above Q). In this mode, NVDA will report any key that you press. If you press an NVDA command (such as NVDA+tab), it will report that. Keys pressed and commands are not executed. This can be a great way of exploring a new keyboard layout. Press NVDA+1 again to turn input help off. Report keystroke: While we’re on help for individual keys, the Report Keystroke command tells you the keystroke to access the currently focussed control. Press shift+numpad 2 (laptop: NVDA+control+shift+dot ) to report the keystroke for the current control .

The WebAIM screen reader user’s survey is on again. This is the 11th edition of the survey, which is the largest survey we are aware of which collects data on screen reader usage and trends. We encourage everyone to complete it in order to give the community as accurate a picture of how you use a screen reader as possible!

The one question I’d like to highlight is “ Screen reader satisfaction ”. Please do answer all the questions honestly, including that one – but if there is anything which makes you think “I’m not 100% satisfied with NVDA” – please let us know! You can create an issue on GitHub (and we’ve previously included GitHub instructions here in In-Process , you can email us , reach us in the official NVDA mailing list , or on social media .

We are very grateful to all our donors . They are one of the main reasons we are able to continue to provide NVDA for free to anyone who can use it anywhere in the world.

This week, we’d like to give a shoutout to Acapela who make the popular Acapela TTS for NVDA . If you are interested in trying Acapela out, they offer an evaluation version which is fully functional and provides access to all voices and all functionalities for 15 days.

Acapela, along with many other options, are listed on our Extra Voices page .

And, if you would like to donate and help keep NVDA free for everyone, we would welcome your support. Please visit our donation page for PayPal or bank donation options. You can also become a GitHub Sponsor .

One of the fixes in the recent NVDA 2026.2 betas is a fix to moving by sentences in Microsoft Word. In many places in Microsoft Office, you can press alt+down arrow to move to the next sentence and alt+up arrow to move to the previous sentence. While this is a feature of Office, if you appreciate moving by sentence and would like to be able to use it everywhere, try out the “ Sentence Nav ” add-on in the add-on store.

Want more ways of getting around? How about: Word ( control+left arrow and control+right arrow ) Paragraph ( control+up arrow and control+down arrow OR shift+p and p ) And as an added bonus for paragraph navigation, here’s a related feature: Paragraph style , which lets you change how NVDA moves when moving by paragraph Single letter navigation What other ways do you prefer to navigate documents? Continue the conversation on social media .

That’s all for this week. Next time around we’ll be close to the final 2026.2 release, so for now, do try out the latest beta and be sure to report any issues. Also don’t forget to do the WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey .

es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 10 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la décima beta de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la décima beta de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 10 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de ampliación, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y capacidades mejoradas de voz y braille. El ampliador proporciona opciones de zoom y filtro de color para asistir a usuarios con baja visión. Actualmente, el ampliador sólo soporta el modo a pantalla completa, dejando los modos acoplados planificados para una futura versión. Se ha expandido significativamente el soporte táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizcar y con navegación en modo exploración táctil en contenido web. Ahora se puede navegar por enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos usando deslizamientos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con soporte de diccionarios del habla personalizados que pueden proporcionarse en complementos y nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que proporcionan un control más granular. Se ha añadido una nueva opción en las voces OneCore para controlar las pausas después de la puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la capacidad de mostrarla en un mensaje explorable. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información verbalizada es NVDA+x, y se puede cambiar desde el diálogo Gestos de entrada. La pantalla braille ahora puede desplazarse automáticamente, y los dispositivos DotPad soportan combinaciones multibotón. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer NVDA a los valores de fábrica, ahora hay disponible un botón de deshacer para restaurar la configuración anterior. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.2 beta 10 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 027c1b5a1d6024288ffc672f601069856aaa75de1b8600ce40ce5beceb623306. ¡Feliz jueves!

La entrada Ya disponible la décima beta de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

Se trata de un escáner portátil de la marca Brother , capaz de digitalizar hojas sueltas y que incorpora funciones como escaneo mediante Wifi, almacenamiento en tarjetas de memoria y una aplicación de gestión con un notable nivel de accesibilidad.

Con motivo del próximo eclipse total de Sol del 12 de agosto se conversa con Enrique Pérez Montero, astrofísico del Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía en Granada, quien comentará algunos de los aspectos más interesantes de este fenómeno astronómico. en.title: In-Process 20th July 2026
en.summary: Welcome to a new week and a new edition of the blog! There’s a few things inside, starting off with very sad news of the passing of a legend of the community. Vale Rui Fontes NVDA 2026.2 Beta 7 Characters per line Introducing Access Point System Accessibility Repair Tool Vale Rui Fontes Last week, we… Read More
en.body:
Welcome to a new week and a new edition of the blog! There’s a few things inside, starting off with very sad news of the passing of a legend of the community.

Last week, we were saddened to receive news of the passing of longtime friend of the NVDA community, and of NV Access, Rui Fontes. Rui was a prominent face of “Tiflotecnia”, the organisation who sell Vocalizer for NVDA. Rui was a very prominent add-on developer. There are 16 current add-ons in the store published by him, including the very popular SysTrayList, ClipSpeak and TesseractOCR being just three, as well as contributing to numerous others. Rui was also very active in the NVDA user group, add-on group and other forums, and very interested in helping people in general, not only with his products. He was a tireless advocate for the community. He will be greatly missed. His family have asked for privacy at this time. Please also refrain from asking about his add-ons. Rest assured, they will continue to work throughout the NVDA 2026.x year cycle, even without any additional updates. No doubt, accommodations will be made for their future long before NVDA 2027.1 comes out, and we will share any additional news as we receive it.

Over the weekend, the community received a message from Rui’s wife and daughters deeply thank all those who expressed their condolences regarding the passing of their beloved one, who will remain eternally in our memories. Be sure to subscribe to the official NVDA users email group , or the add-on group for updates and other community news.

Once again, we are a couple of betas – three in fact – further along than we were last time the blog came out. Let’s see what’s new in NVDA 2026.2 Beta 7 :

Changes introduced in Beta 7: Updates to translations Fix NVDA prompting to restart after updating, instead of logging off Revert SAPI5 bug fix from beta6 which was causing issues loading synthesizers Fix reading PDF content in Foxit PDF Editor with browse mode

Changes introduced in Beta 6: Updates to translations Show the restart dialog after updating from within NVDA, and make sure restarting offers the user the ability to save work in progress SAPI5 bug fix: skip over invalid voices rather than causing the entire driver to fail SAPI4 32-bit bug fix: support voices that don’t support pitch or rate Improve conflict handling between magnifier and screen curtain Restore the ability for add-ons to register custom touch modes in availableTouchModes

Changes introduced in Beta 5: Updates to translations Use math navigation category for one more math script Prevent NVDA freeze when brailling math with certain Unicode characters Improvements to Magnifier messages and settings names

Do head to the NVDA 2026.2 Beta 7 release announcement and try out the new beta. In fact, work is progressing well and we expect another beta to come out in the next few days.

We were recently asked about the “ Maximum Number of Characters on One Line ” setting. What does it do? And when might you change it?

Screenshot of NVDA’s browse mode settings

Ok, firstly, what is it? In a Word document or notepad text, the program exposes how much text is on one line. If you press down arrow, the caret moves to the character directly below. On the web, this isn’t as clearly defined. The size of the window, CSS rules, JavaScript, nearby images, and many other things can affect exactly how much text fits on a line. Because of this, and the way screen readers process web content, the document does not expose exactly where to move when you press down arrow. The way we work around this is to arbitrarily decide how many characters are on a “line”. There is a setting in NVDA’s browse mode settings called “Maximum number of characters on one line”. The default value for this is 100 characters. That is, when you press “down arrow”, the caret moves forward through the text on the web page by 100 characters.

As an example, the first line of the latest beta release announcement, visually, is: “Beta7 of NVDA 2026.2 is now available for download and testing. For” At NVDA’s default 100 max characters per line, pressing down arrow to that line will continue on to read “anyone who is interested in”, before stopping. If you change it to 50 chars, it will stop after “Available for” (it avoids stopping at half words).

The Beta 7 release announcement, used in the example above

NVDA user James also added: “When you’re not doing a say all and want to press Down Arrow less often, increase it. When you’re not doing a say all and would find it easier to process text in smaller chunks, decrease it.” Fellow NVDA user Pratik offered: “I have it set to maximum most times as well. If I want to read in smaller chunks, I do it with my Braille display. It’s a nice compromise.”

There is a companion setting, “Maximum lines per page” which, you can probably guess, adjusts how many lines the caret moves when you press page up or page down. The default for this is 25 lines.

How do you have these options set? Do continue the conversation on the Mastodon thread , or in the user group .

World Services for the Blind in the United States is one of many organisations around the world who provide training in NVDA. This is a valuable part of the job readiness program they provide. They recently invited us to collaborate with them on a webinar series introducing the new features of NVDA around the time of each release. We are very pleased to share with you, the inaugural “Access Point” webinar, with a focus on NVDA 2026.1 . We know many of our regular readers will be very familiar with what was new in NVDA 2026.1, as it has been out for nearly a couple of months now, but if you’d like a refresher, this could be the webinar for you. Starting something new always takes a little time to dial in, so we anticipate having the next version out a lot closer to when the stable NVDA 2026.2 is released.

We don’t often update features in ways which don’t change how they work. And, when we do, we don’t often highlight it. But let’s make an exception! NVDA has had a tool called the “COM registration fixing tool” for a long time now. We have covered it once before , and at the time noted that it could fix issues including: NVDA reports “unknown” when navigating in browsers such as Firefox, Thunderbird etc NVDA fails to switch between focus mode and browse mode NVDA is very slow when navigating in browsers while using browse mode

The tool can still fix all those and more, and it works much the same – but now it has a new name. Introducing: “System Accessibility Repair Tool”. The tool is a useful troubleshooting step any time you run into an unusual problem with NVDA. It is also one of the steps you are encouraged to make before reporting an issue on GitHub.

You can still find the System Accessibility Repair Tool on NVDA’s “Tools” menu. Press NVDA+n , then t for tools and you’ll find it listed there.
